narrative: The causal analysis using LinearDML estimates an average treatment effect (ATE) of 0.01 (95% CI: [-0.01, 0.02]). This effect is classified as small and is not statistically significant. The effect passed 3 out of 4 robustness tests, indicating the finding is likely genuine and not spurious. No detectable effect at this sample size. The 95 % CI [-0.005, 0.019] includes zero at n = 15209. The estimate is reported as a null finding; no unmeasured confounder is needed to explain it. Because the treatment dupixent → discontinued 180d effect is not yet significant and/or robust, hold off on acting on it: enlarge the cohort or extend the window to gain power, and re-run with an alternative adjustment set and a placebo outcome before making a strategic call.
executive_summary: The estimated effect is 0.007 (small), but it is not statistically significant (3/4 robustness checks passed). Treat this as preliminary; overall confidence: low.
recommendations: Do not act on treatment dupixent → discontinued 180d for this brand yet: the effect is not yet distinguishable from zero and/or did not clear the robustness gate — treating it as real risks spending against noise.
Increase statistical power: enlarge the this brand cohort or extend the observation window, then re-estimate treatment dupixent → discontinued 180d before making a call.
Pressure-test the design: re-run with an alternative adjustment set and a placebo outcome; a genuine treatment dupixent → discontinued 180d effect should survive, a spurious one will not.
key_insights: E-value: 1.33 — No detectable effect at this sample size
